summary: MaterialDNA maintenance.repairCount currently validates finite non-negative integer shape but has no IEEE-754 safe-integer ceiling. Canonical count state must accept 9007199254740991 (2^53-1) and reject 9007199254740992 (2^53) to prevent non-exact counter identities without schema/version churn.
evidence: src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateNonNegativeInteger checks type, finiteness, non-negativity, and floor equality only, then maintenance.repairCount uses that helper without a maximum.
The exact IEEE-754 safe-integer boundary is 9007199254740991; 9007199254740992 is integer-shaped in a double but cannot participate in exact +1 counter semantics.
Regression coverage should use explicit boundary literals, preserving all existing fixture recipe identities/fingerprints and avoiding a new identity or migration framework.
